source.title: A real-world study of immune thrombocytopenia management during the COVID-19 pandemic in the UK

source_integrity_findings: Table I labels the overall column n=343 and reports 23/343 positive COVID-19 tests, while the Results section defines the eligible cohort as n=335 and separately reports 23/335 overall; the tested subgroup denominator is 243.
Table I prints post-COVID-19 vaccination as 0/3 (100%) in the maintenance-therapy column, which is arithmetically inconsistent with the numerator and denominator.

Table II reports fourth-line treatment in 33/172 corticosteroid cases (19.2%) even though the overall fourth-line row is 20/295 (6.8%), and the prednisolone and dexamethasone fourth-line subrows sum to 10 cases.

The Table II thrombosis footnote says there were seven venous thromboses but then enumerates three deep vein thromboses, four pulmonary embolisms, one portal vein thrombosis, and one sinus venous thrombosis, which totals nine venous events.
The Results prose states that 23/30 second-line TPO-RA cases avoided third-line treatment at 76.1%, whereas Figure S1 prints 23/30 as 76.7%.

The article and Table S1 report 76/335 secondary ITP as 22.3%, although that fraction is approximately 22.7%; Table S1 also contains a drug-induced row of 6/78 despite the stated secondary-ITP total of 76.
schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom quantitative_result sufficiency rule requires exposures even for descriptive cohort statistics. Cohort-wide descriptive results therefore use an explicit observational study-context exposure and are tagged as non-randomized context.
extraction_limitations: No external bibliographic or current-practice verification was performed because @VERIFY was not activated.
Figure S2 does not print numeric values on individual bars, so only its qualitative temporal pattern was extracted.
The source contains internal denominator and arithmetic inconsistencies; they were retained and flagged rather than repaired.
